- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price drop is sharp.  
- After a price spike (forecast > true > 5% above recent mean), model overcorrects; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after peak or rises after dip), model often lags; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the cycle; apply 2–4% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model fails to anticipate turn; add 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment flips.
